speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs regarding allegations in the report of the Special Advisory Council for Myanmar dated 16 January 2023 claiming that Singapore functions as a "strategic transit point for potentially significant volumes of items" including raw materials that contribute towards military production by the Myanmar military, whether the Government will carry out a check on all Singaporean companies, including companies that may be implicated by the report, to ensure compliance with the prohibitions against the transfer of items having potential military application in Myanmar against civilians.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is also worth emphasising that before the military coup, there was a legitimate government in Myanmar whom we fully recognised and whom we had constructive, comprehensive relations with.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Specifically on military sales, I want to quote former Minister for Foreign Affairs George Yeo when he answered the question in 2007 on whether Singapore has supplied arms to Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: He said: "As far as defence sales are concerned, it is established policy of the Government not to divulge details publicly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Myanmar is not subject to any UN arms embargo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If there is any UN sanction against Myanmar, Singapore will of course abide by it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the declaration of arms exports, Singapore submits regular reports to the UN Register of Conventional Arms (UNROCA).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In June 2021, Singapore also voted in favour of UN General Assembly Resolution 75/287 entitled "The Situation in Myanmar".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This resolution called on the UN member states to "prevent the flow of arms into Myanmar".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will not hesitate to take action against those who contravene our laws, including Singapore's Strategic Goods (Control) Act which controls the transfer and brokering of strategic goods and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore remains committed to working with the fellow ASEAN member states and UN member states to facilitate peace and national reconciliation in Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I can only hope this comes sooner rather than later.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: First, I would like to ask the Minister what checks were carried out after the allegations were made in the special report in respect of Singaporean companies?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And secondly, what measures are put in place by the Government to check on Singaporean companies on a regular basis in respect of their compliance or does the Government only follow up when there is a feedback or complaint on any non-compliance?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On the first supplementary question on what checks were made, I looked at the assertions of the Special Advisory Council.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I said, in fact, most of those assertions go way back in time – some were more than 20 years ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, within the limited access which I have now after two decades, what I can say, looking at Mr George Yeo's response is that we have maintained that same position and, therefore, there have been no defence sales for a very long time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are talking more than a decade, decade and a half.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And you must remember that that also includes the transshipment of arms.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is effected legally through our Strategic Goods (Control) Act.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that means we go through every submission of an import/export.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If clearly there are military items there, we are going to flag up a red flag.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Where they are dual-use items, civilian items – but which in our judgement would also pose risks to unarmed civilians, we will also flag a red flag.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am informing you and I am also putting all companies on notice that we are taking a very firm line on this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think Members in this House will share our sympathy for the unarmed civilians in Myanmar and we want to make sure that nothing we do aggravates the situation there.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am sure this is something which enjoys the Member's support and that of the Member's party as well.
